purpose: Record independently reviewable source candidates before any physical values are promoted into the canonical table.
approval_rule: No candidate is an approved production source until the source file, license, citation, conversion procedure, checksum, and channel-specific closure report are present.
candidate_package_fingerprint_scheme: sha256(candidate_id + NUL + sorted UTF-8 records path + NUL + bytes + NUL + file_sha256 + LF); manifest-scoped review fingerprint only; not a redistribution/package identity claim; F-P1 admission instead requires the executable source-identity validator composite fingerprint

review_selection.parked_disposition: Retain raw data and review readers; no author contact, automatic re-review, value correction or production promotion. Resume only for an explicitly requested source decision. Does not block source-independent native RT/feedback/dust engineering.
review_selection.basis: First engine-specific solar-metallicity validation branch for the 40--120 Msun terminal-fate seam; W18/N20 outcomes remain source-comparison evidence and do not define a production fate law.

candidates.citation: Jost et al. 2025, Neutrino-driven core-collapse supernova yields in Galactic chemical evolution

reported_coverage.zams_mass_msun: 11--30 in 1 Msun steps at primordial, 1e-4 solar, and solar metallicity; 35, 40, and 75 Msun at solar metallicity only
reported_coverage.release_time_grid: terminal explosion/ejecta outcomes, not an age-resolved wind history

candidates.known_gap_for_this_project: The source leaves the runtime 8--11 Msun transition uncovered, is not a cumulative wind+AGB+SNII Cartesian grid, and must be converted without double counting pre-SN winds. The OUP issue/article record confirms that Supplementary data exist, but the dynamically hosted publisher package could not be retrieved and fingerprinted; Crossref and the arXiv source package do not contain the yield asset. No values may be reconstructed from article tables or figures.

candidates.citation: Boccioli & Roberti 2026, Explodability matters: How realistic neutrino-driven explosions change explosive nucleosynthesis yields

reported_coverage.f23_single_mass_msun: 11--45 in 1 Msun steps at source-labelled solar metallicity
reported_coverage.f23_binary_mass_msun: 11--45 with missing 24,25,28,29 Msun nodes at source-labelled solar metallicity
reported_coverage.wh07_mass_msun: 12--120 at solar metallicity with a nonuniform high-mass grid
reported_coverage.release_products: stable and 30-s no-decay isotope yields, element yields, integrated winds, pre-SN inventories, mass cuts, and explosion outcomes

physics_to_record: emergent baryonic mass cut with no fallback for successful explosions
candidates.known_gap_for_this_project: The F23 single branch closes its released component masses and improves candidate SNII coverage to 11--40 Msun, but it is solar-only. The release has no machine-readable per-model explosion energy, canonical momentum, or age-resolved cumulative history. The LC18 branch has a release inconsistency: all 56 failed models retain positive summary wind masses but their Wind tables are zero, contrary to the README's failed-model policy. The runtime 8--11 Msun transition and the single/binary population weighting remain unresolved.

candidates.citation: Limongi & Chieffi 2018, Presupernova evolution and explosive nucleosynthesis of rotating massive stars

reported_coverage.release_history: terminal yields plus lifetime/properties scalars; no age-resolved cumulative grid

candidates.known_gap_for_this_project: The article resolves set-R semantics: 13--25 Msun table8 includes wind plus terminal ejecta, table9 is wind, and table8 above 25 Msun is wind-only. The source still does not cover the complete runtime wind 0.8--120 or SNII 8--40 ranges; project channel approval, energy, momentum, and release history remain missing.

reported_coverage.release_history: integrated total/wind/pre-explosion yields plus lifetime scalar; no age-resolved cumulative grid

candidates.known_gap_for_this_project: The article resolves the files as wind-only, wind plus pre-SN ejecta, and wind plus delayed-explosion SN ejecta. The table still has a duplicate (5 Msun, Z=0.01) coordinate, mass gaps, no canonical per-channel energy/momentum fields, no age-resolved wind history, and incomplete runtime coverage.

candidates.citation: Huscher, Finlator & Jackiewicz 2025, Asymptotic Giant Branch Mass-loss Rates and Metal Yields from Scaled Mixing-length and Mass-loss Parameters

reported_coverage.population_tables: IMF-weighted Mdot and outflow C12/N14/O16 mass fractions at 153 log-age nodes

candidates.known_gap_for_this_project: The per-star grid ends at 7 Msun, has only 16 isotopes and no S/Ca/Fe, and is lifetime-integrated. Direct physical-time integration of the population Mdot table under its README units returns 1326--2895 Msun per claimed Msun formed; its hidden normalization must be clarified rather than guessed. Energy and momentum are absent.

candidates.citation: Doherty et al. 2014, Super and massive AGB stars II and III

reported_coverage.release_products: gross and net integrated SAGB wind yields plus synthetic-pulse and mass-loss sensitivity branches

candidates.known_gap_for_this_project: The baseline VW93 wind branch narrows the 7--8 Msun AGB gap, but Z<=0.001 stops at 7.5 Msun, calcium and per-star age histories are absent, and terminal ECSN/Fe-core outcomes are outside this release. The alternate table's literal al-6 label is preserved rather than guessed. Redistribution terms are not explicit.

candidates.citation: Stockinger et al. 2020, Three-dimensional Models of Core-collapse Supernovae From Low-mass Progenitors With Implications for Crab

reported_coverage.release_products: three post-bounce yield snapshots per model and machine-readable diagnostic explosion-energy time series

candidates.known_gap_for_this_project: These three physically heterogeneous models are discrete anchors and cannot be interpolated into a continuous 8--11 Msun grid. Nitrogen is absent, radioactive/tracer projection is unresolved, the vsh unit attribute is invalid and quarantined, canonical momentum is absent, and third-party redistribution requires MPA archive permission.

candidates.citation: Sukhbold et al. 2016, Core-collapse Supernovae from 9 to 120 Solar Masses Based on Neutrino-powered Explosions

reported_coverage.reviewed_engine: Z9.6 Crab-calibrated P-HOTB; all 13 reviewed models explode
reported_coverage.release_products: P-HOTB final kinetic energy, fallback, and baryonic mass cut plus KEPLER gross stable-isotope explosion/wind yields and 20 selected radioactive isotopes

candidates.known_gap_for_this_project: The 9--12 Msun Z9.6 grid closes the previous candidate source-hull gap between Stockinger and F23, but it does not cover 8--9 Msun or define a metallicity axis. The stable and selected-radioactive segments are not a complete decay inventory, neutrino-powered wind nucleosynthesis and canonical momentum are absent, presupernova winds are not age resolved, and third-party redistribution requires archive permission.

candidates.citation: Limongi et al. 2024, Evolution and Final Fate of Solar Metallicity Stars in the Mass Range 7--15 Msun. I

reported_coverage.release_products: article fate statements and a 963-row thermal-pulse property table; no terminal event yields

candidates.known_gap_for_this_project: This source proves that the runtime 8 Msun SNII lower boundary is not a universal physical explosion threshold. Its 8.5--9.2 Msun models may potentially undergo ECSN after extrapolated thermal-pulse evolution, and the inferred lower edge shifts from about 8.5--8.8 to about 8.3 Msun with the adopted electron-capture core-mass criterion. It supplies no yields, energy, momentum, or continuous fate law; the 8--8.8 Msun production edge remains blocked.

candidates.citation: Roberti, Limongi & Chieffi 2024, Zero and Extremely Low-metallicity Rotating Massive Stars: Evolution, Explosion, and Nucleosynthesis

reported_coverage.release_products: evolutionary properties, integrated explosive isotopic yields, source-table remnant masses and kinetic energies

candidates.known_gap_for_this_project: This is the first staged source with coordinates near the inherited ultra-low-Z comparison population, but it has only 15 and 25 Msun models. Four zero-Z article columns are absent from the official MRTs, 025z600 has a 12.48 Msun mass-budget discrepancy, wind and terminal components are not separated, and neither mass/metallicity interpolation nor a rotation population is approved. Its coordinate hull is not production coverage.

candidates.citation: Heger & Woosley 2010, Nucleosynthesis and Evolution of Massive Metal-Free Stars

reported_coverage.release_products: 660546 official VizieR isotopic-ejecta rows including fallback; terminal integrated release only

physics_to_record: kinetic energy at infinity rather than central-engine deposition energy
candidates.known_gap_for_this_project: The source materially improves exact-Z=0 mass coverage but starts at 10 Msun while the runtime SNII channel starts at 8 Msun, and it has no positive-metallicity axis. Explosion energy, piston, and artificial-mixing population distributions are unselected; rotation and neutrino-wind nucleosynthesis are omitted; remnant mass is not an explicit machine-readable column; no age-resolved release or canonical momentum is supplied. Scientific use is verified through VizieR, but public redistribution terms are not.

candidates.citation: Karakas & Lugaro 2016, Stellar yields from metal-rich asymptotic giant branch models

reported_coverage.release_time_grid: integrated lifetime ejecta; thermal-pulse surface histories are separate products

source_row_review.initial_z007_header_findings: Repeated 1.5 Msun header and no 7.5 Msun header; no positional repair or substitution.
source_row_review.element_identity: Atomic number, not source symbol: p labels both hydrogen (1) and phosphorus (15).
source_row_review.gross_definition: Lifetime-integrated elemental ejecta in Msun; not IMF-weighted (KL16 section 4).
source_row_review.decay_semantics: KL16 section 3 assumes radioactive isotopes decayed in yield tables, unlike its surface-abundance tables; no second decay transform is applied.
source_row_review.net_definition: gross - initial mass fraction * labelled expelled mass; diagnostic only at unique full-header matches, otherwise null. Negative net values are retained.
source_row_review.publication_table7_match: Six visible gross-yield entries for 3.5 Msun, Z=0.03 match the paper exactly; this is not whole-supplement authentication.

candidates.known_gap_for_this_project: COLIBRE author's mirror contains 64 model headers over the three published Z values; the two 8 Msun yield blocks at Z=0.014 and 0.03 are commented out and absent from its auxiliary mass arrays. All 64 blocks including those commented records contain the eleven tracked elements, but a descriptive sum of listed gross masses differs from the labelled expelled mass by up to 0.035693969 Msun (maximum relative difference 0.0058363335). Do not uncomment, renormalize or accept these as qualified nodes without source-specific reconciliation. Per-star ages, release ownership, energy, physical population choice and rights remain unresolved.

candidates.citation: Cinquegrana & Karakas 2022, The most metal-rich stars in the universe: chemical contributions of low- and intermediate-mass AGB stars

reported_coverage.zams_mass_msun: 1--8 in 0.5 Msun steps except two source-excluded nodes
reported_coverage.release_time_grid: integrated net and gross isotope ejecta, not per-star age-resolved release

physics_to_record: distinct net and gross yield columns
candidates.known_gap_for_this_project: No Ca rows, no Z=0.10--0.139 support, two explicitly omitted mass/Z nodes. Eight gross entries are tiny negative values, maximum magnitude 6.9439942e-29 Msun; no source bytes or values were repaired. Maximum net-(gross-initial) residual is 9e-8 Msun, a descriptive check not full mass closure. Do not use the COLIBRE processed HDF5 as raw support: its converter extends masses to 12 Msun and assigns surrogate heavy-element yields. No canonical rows or physical approval.

evolution_reference.citation: Karakas, Cinquegrana & Joyce 2022, MNRAS 509, 4430; arXiv:2111.01308v1, Tables 2--4
evolution_reference.meaning: Preserve published tau_stellar and phase durations in Myr, including duplicate 5 Msun Z=0.08 rows. Mc(1) is first-thermal-pulse core mass, NOT final remnant mass. Duration is not an approved instantaneous release age; some sequences terminate early.

source_row_review.column_semantics_caveat: Source header <X(i)> follows the K10 mean-wind convention; CK22 README calls it final mass fraction. Do not substitute for a surface abundance. mass(i)_0 is initial-composition mass in the expelled wind, not initial stellar mass times X0.

candidates.citation: Osborn et al. 2025, Using Binary Population Synthesis to Calculate the Yields of Low- and Intermediate-Mass Binary Populations at Low Metallicity
candidates.known_gap_for_this_project: Single low-metallicity point is not sufficient for the required metallicity grid; binary population assumptions must match the selected stellar SED/IMF.

candidates.citation: Keegans et al. 2023, Type Ia Supernova Nucleosynthesis: Metallicity-Dependent Yields

reported_coverage.progenitor_families: 1.4 Msun deflagration-detonation, 1.0 and 0.8 Msun double detonation
reported_coverage.event_release: single-event ejecta; DTD convolution remains separate

candidates.known_gap_for_this_project: This cannot be loaded as an ordinary 3--8 Msun IMF channel; a separately approved SNIa DTD and binary normalization are required.
The current switch must not infer PISN from a universal ZAMS 140--260 Msun interval.
A CCSN table's pre-SN mass loss cannot be silently reused as an independent wind channel; a dedicated source or explicit partition is required.
